message.content: {"criteria":[{"id":"C1","level":"Accomplished","mark":8,"evidence":[{"where":"Introduction","quote":"Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring."},{"where":"Introduction","quote":"Thus, only one satellite is required."},{"where":"Introduction","quote":"The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)"}],"reasoning":"Mission purpose, rationale, single-spacecraft justification and users are all addressed with literature support. Rationale is persuasive; operator/customer distinction is somewhat loose but adequate for high standard."},{"id":"C2","level":"Adequate","mark":6,"evidence":[{"where":"Orbit","quote":"an altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 97.7924°"},{"where":"Ground Control & Communications","quote":"An average contact duration of almost ten minutes was achieved"},{"where":"Mission Duration & EOL","quote":"The proposed ZYZZsat is small and without thrusters in a low-earth orbit."}],"reasoning":"All major elements covered with STK screenshots and access data. However, launch choice is speculative (Vega E not yet built), RAAN/launch-site consistency is questionable, no hand calculations for J2 or delta-v, and EOL drag-sail discussion is incomplete. Evidence present but not fully rigorous."},{"id":"C3","level":"Adequate","mark":6,"evidence":[{"where":"Conclusion","quote":"A specific launch vehicle – the Vega E – has been selected although it has not been built yet."}],"reasoning":"Conclusion summarises design and acknowledges launch risk, but is largely generic and lacks quantitative outcomes or explicit EOL/coverage conclusions."},{"id":"C4","level":"Adequate","mark":5,"evidence":[{"where":"Bibliography","quote":"[5] f. https://www.qrg.northwestern.edu"},{"where":"Bibliography","quote":"[6] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_in_spaceflight"},{"where":"Orbit","quote":"[Image 1]"}],"reasoning":"Structure and headings are clear, but references are bare URLs, one is Wikipedia, citation formatting is inconsistent, figures lack numbered captions, and there are typos/awkward phrasing. launch geometry not demonstrated."},{"where":"Orbit","issue":"Inclination 97.79° for 600 km SSO is plausible, but no hand calculation of J2 nodal precession shown; only a plot."},{"where":"Launch","issue":"Selecting Vega E (first launch 2024, unproven) for a 2025 mission is high risk; no delta-v or payload mass analysis."},{"where":"Ground Control & Communications","issue":"Access table has duplicate row 15 and inconsistent date formatting; mean duration stated as ~10 min but table mean is 580.8 s (~9.7 min), acceptable but rounding unclear."},{"where":"Mission Duration & EOL","issue":"Drag sail discussion truncated; no deorbit time estimate or casualty risk assessment; statement that satellite is 'without thrusters' conflicts with earlier mention of orbital manoeuvre at EOL."},{"where":"Orbit","issue":"Swath/altitude trade not quantified; 600 km choice not supported by resolution calculation."}],"overall":"A competent, well-structured report covering all mission elements with STK evidence, but weakened by speculative launch choice, unverified orbital geometry, missing hand calculations, poor referencing (including Wikipedia) and incomplete EOL analysis. Adequate overall."}
